items.stem: Rent for a factory building is fixed at $60,000 per year regardless of output. How is this cost best classified by behaviour?

options.rationale: Correct: a cost that does not change with the level of activity over the period is a fixed cost.
A variable cost changes with activity; this rent does not.
A semi-variable cost has both fixed and variable elements; flat rent has only a fixed element.
A stepped cost jumps at activity thresholds; the rent stays flat here.

items.explanation: Correct: a cost that does not change with the level of activity over the period is a fixed cost.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A company uses 2,000 kg of material costing $5 per kg in a month. Which total direct material cost should be recorded?

options.rationale: Correct: 2,000 kg x $5 = $10,000 of direct material cost.
This divides quantity by price and is not a cost total.
This adds the quantity and price instead of multiplying them.
This uses only half the quantity.

items.explanation: Correct: 2,000 kg x $5 = $10,000 of direct material cost.

items.stem: Select TWO benefits of using a logical cost-coding system in a management information system.

options.text: Costs can be collected and reported consistently by category
options.rationale: Correct: codes let similar costs be grouped and reported consistently.

options.text: Data entry and analysis can be processed more quickly and with fewer errors
options.rationale: Correct: structured codes speed processing and reduce misclassification.

options.text: It removes the need to keep any source documents
options.rationale: Source documents are still required as evidence; coding does not replace them.

options.text: It guarantees the business will make a profit
options.rationale: Coding organises information; it does not determine profitability.

options.text: It replaces the need for a trial balance
options.rationale: Coding does not replace the trial balance or the double-entry system.

items.explanation: Correct: codes let similar costs be grouped and reported consistently.
